items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
In sixteen thirty-seven, legend says a single tulip bulb cost as much as a house in Amsterdam.
Narrator
The star was the Semper Augustus: white petals with flames of red.
Narrator
Its price climbed from about twelve hundred guilders to a reported ten thousand.
Narrator
People traded bulbs still in the ground, on paper contracts in taverns.
Narrator
Then, in February sixteen thirty-seven, at an auction in Haarlem, nobody bid. Within a week, prices collapsed.
Narrator
The story says the Dutch economy was ruined. Families lost everything.
Narrator
But here's the twist. Historian Anne Goldgar searched the records and couldn't find anyone who went bankrupt.
Narrator
Much of the drama comes from a book written two hundred years later.
Narrator
That's the mirage: history's most famous bubble was partly a bubble of a story.
Narrator
So when you hear everyone lost everything, check who's telling it.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
